root_cause: release.json used the exact deployment SHA but the final built HTML was not re-stamped after all page transformers, so live-contract readback saw an older bg-release-commit marker.
The mobile i18n injector only supported aside.v18-mobile-drawer, while pricing can use the compact #bgkopMob/.bgkop-mob drawer, leaving no visible mobile language select.

The compact-drawer repair accidentally embedded a second function body inside a single-quoted HTML replacement string in tools/site-shell/apply-i18n.mjs, producing a JavaScript syntax error. Existing source-regex tests verified tokens but did not execute or syntax-check the build script, so Netlify failed with build exit code 2.
prevention: Stamp every final built HTML document with ensureReleaseMarker(html, commitRef) in the last release-evidence boundary.
Mobile language injection must support every canonical public mobile drawer variant and remain data-bg-no-translate.
Build-time JavaScript transformers changed by recovery work must pass node --check and an executable fixture test; source-token regex assertions alone are insufficient.
Compact mobile injection must prepend MOBILE_LANGUAGE with a replacement callback, never concatenate generated JavaScript source into HTML replacement text.
Terminal production truth requires release.json exact SHA, HTML release marker exact SHA, successful provider build, pricing interaction proof, and NL→EN→NL browser roundtrip.

evidence.failed_step: Deploy exact source through authorized Netlify transport
